chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is not for the women from the center of the road, but on its sides, meaning the middle [is for men/others].'
ai.seo_question: Where should women walk according to this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* outlines the juristic principle of *haya* (modesty) by directing women to occupy the periphery of public thoroughfares, thereby minimizing interaction with men and preserving social decorum. Scholars interpret this as a practical application of modesty in urban settings, emphasizing that while not a strict prohibition, it is a recommended etiquette to avoid the center where male traffic is typically denser. This ruling reflects the broader Shia emphasis on contextual modesty rather than rigid segregation, focusing on the preservation of dignity in public spaces.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘It is not for the women from the centre of the road, meaning its middle, but to its sides’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Women must not walk in the Surat (center) of the road but they must walk on either side - it (surat) is the middle of it.’”
